answer: A sealed agent registry can harbor identity proofs as tamper-evident borescope images logged per inspection cycle. Each new agent submits a prism of hardware-attested keys and repair-history hashes, and cross-agent consensus rejects duplicates like a borescope spotting a hairline crack before failure. The wharf of admission costs an attacker a fresh attested device and bonded stake per identity, capping farms at the cost of physical hardware, though compromised genuine devices still slip through.
